Apple reported research and development spending climbed to a record $11.73 billion in its quarterly earnings, continuing the sharp upward trend seen throughout fiscal year 2026. Here are the details.

Apple Ramps Up R&D Spending

Last quarter, Apple reported R&D spending of $11.4 billion, up 34% year over year.

On the company's earnings call, Tim Cook said Apple was "clearly investing more," and added that R&D spending was growing "at a much higher rate than the company overall."

He went on to reiterate that R&D spending had "expanded quite significantly" on a year-over-year basis, particularly when speaking about Apple's AI investments. Apple CFO Kevan Parekh also added that AI-related spending is incrementally stacking on top of Apple's normal product roadmap investments.

Apple today reported fiscal Q3 2026 earnings with R&D spending hitting a new record of $11.73 billion, up 32% from the same quarter last year, bringing Apple's total R&D spending for fiscal year 2026 so far to $34.04 billion.

For comparison, Apple spent $34.55 billion on R&D during the entirety of fiscal year 2025. That means the company has nearly matched last year's full-year total with one quarter still remaining, while also having already surpassed the full-year R&D spend for fiscal years 2024 and 2023.

Over the past few days, Wall Street has punished companies that announced accelerated AI-related spending without showing equally clear near-term returns.

Alphabet's stock price fell 7% as the company raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast by $15 billion, to a range between $195 billion and $205 billion. Meta's stock also dropped roughly 9% to 10% as free cash flow plunged 91%, while raising the lower bound of its full-year capex forecast to $130 billion.

Apple's stock is currently down about 4% in after-hours trading. That reaction could shift again during the earnings call and again during normal trading hours tomorrow.
